notes.title: TOING'S POPS UPDATE 2 IS OUT NOW
notes.content:
UPDATE 2

In update 2 I added a bunch of fun stuff, and helpful bits and bobs.
I added objectives, updated music, updated gameplay, improved performance, improved graphics, updated textures, updated title screen, new SFX, new VFX, updated models, made new models, and much more for you to find ;)

notes.title: Toing's Pops Update 2
notes.content:
With Toing's Pops 2 (was originally a DLC but ended up being too big) in full development, I thought I should improve the first game as well. There are a lot of things that people have given feedback on that I worked on in this update, and also some things that I personally felt the game needed. This is stuff like models, and one of the songs from the ost. I also redid a lot of the lighting so the game looks, and performs better.

People have said they're confused while playing, and don't know what to do. I worked on this part a lot, and decided that instead of having this whole tutorial screen that you have to read it should be in the actual world. You will now know from the environment that putting on the glasses reveals hidden stuff, but also makes Toing invisible. I'm also working on an objective system to give you hints on what to do next. I don't want it to hold your hand, but rather to give an idea of what to do.

As for the models, I replaced all of those mesh bins with the candy in them (those were the first model I ever made for the game besides the actual building), and replaced them with something much less terrible. I also made a new model for Bink. He now looks like he has personality and emotion. 


I don't think there's much to specify on about the new lighting, the game looks good. It also performs good. Yeah.


The trailer is linked to this, so give it a watch if you want and give me any feedback if you have any!

It releases October 31st (don't quote me on that)

Oh yeah, also it now says that the game is developed and published by foamy999. RIP Dishsoap Studios 2023-2023. I should probably replace the text in game.

notes.title: Toing's Pops Update 1.1.0
notes.content:
The first big (ish) update of Toing's Pops!


[b]Features[/b]
- Added a new HUD icon for the glasses
- Added a new and much more in depth graphics settings menu, as well as fixing a bug causing graphics settings not to save
- You will have to find this one :O)

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
- Fixed a bug causing the path to not disappear after activating the monitor
- Fixed a bug causing Toing to be half dissolved if you respawned in the back room
- Fixed a bug causing the HUD to disappear after having "Press E to Interact" show up on the player's screen
- Fixed a bug causing the back room to not glow after the second cutscene



Ok not as major as I thought, but The HUD icon update was big for me as I learned how to make UI better!

notes.title: Toing's Pops 1.0.5 Hotfix Patch Notes
notes.content: - I think I fixed the falling through map bug

notes.title: One week of Toing's Pops
notes.content:
It's been one full week since Toing's Pops released. The current rating on Steam is mostly positive, and I could not thank you all enough. I want to make this more of a weekly thing maybe, just giving updates about Toing's Pops and the development of future content in the series and current game. So to start this off, let's discuss the game's stability and some of the loading issues.

Since the release of the game, there's been 4 hotfixes. I'm really happy with the fact that I've been able to fix all of the problems within this week, but I'm not happy about the fact that I let the game release with as many bugs as it did. I understand now why games have bugs because there are so many factors to consider. I'm certainly trying though, remember that this is the first game I have ever made and released. I'm glad to see people are enjoying the game despite the bugs this week. I have also received a lot of feedback about the gameplay, and how it can be very confusing, so I added in a tutorial when you first put on your glasses that tells you how to use them. A lot of the feedback I got was about how people didn't know where to go after you activated the monitor, so I added symbols to follow as well as text that tells you to follow them. I don't want the game to be confusing, but I also don't want it to hold your hand. I'll continue to listen to feedback, and will continue to make changes to improve the experience of the game.

Next I want to talk about an issue that I've heard a lot about: falling through the map. I've encountered this bug a lot during development, but never quite understood how to fix it. The issue is that the player loads before the world does, as does Toing and Bink. I've tried to mitigate this with a loading screen plugin, removing the ability to skip the first and second cutscenes, but I'm still hearing people say that they are falling through the world. I'm still learning, and I originally thought this was only an in-engine problem, but it's now apparent it's a large problem no matter if it's in engine or packaged. I have a few more solutions to try, I'll give updates on this as it goes!

Finally, I want to say thank you. No matter what you think of the game, you've contributed to it's development post-release. Development for a free DLC to expand apon the story is being planned, and development for the second game has begun. I don't have an exact timeline of when the DLC will release, that's something that won't take super long I don't think. As for the second game, I don't have any idea for that either, it's something that's really far out as I want to make it the best it can possibly be. Something completely different and unique from most horror nowadays. I won't give out too much about it though, you'll hear about it when you hear about it. I do not want it to be the same thing in a different location with a number slapped on the cover, like so much of horror is nowadays. 

I'm extremely excited for everything to come, thank you all. I'll keep y'all updated on the upcoming changes and fixes, as well as the DLC.

And as always, go fuck yourself
- Foamy

notes.title: Toing's Pops 1.0.3 Patch Notes
notes.content:
SPOILERS!!

Bug Fixes:
	- Fixed a soft lock where the player would despawn if you didn't enter the shelter within 30 seconds of hitting the machine button
	   - Also lowered the timer to 25 seconds	   
	     - It's now a death with a new sound effect!
	
	- Fixed a bug where Toing wouldn't chase the player inside the back room
	   - He still runs into the corner, that's a bigger bug I'm still trying to solve

QOL and UI Improvements:

	- Added a new glasses tutorial when you press the glasses key for the first time
	- Added text to the first symbol to help mitigate confusion around them
	- Changed the buttons in the title screen
		- They were really ugly

	- Changed the respawn button
		- This one was also really ugly


That's all the fixes (I think?). Wait, no, I forgot to make the TV only play once. Oops, well that'll be fixed in a later patch.

notes.title: Toing's Pops Version 1.0.2 Patch Notes
notes.content:
People were having trouble finding where to go after the kitchen, so I added some symbols to make it less confusing on where to go.
              - Added symbols after the kitchen

I also fixed a bug where the game would soft lock if you were in your esc menu when the game switched levels.

                    - Fixed an issue causing an occasional soft lock after Boing's Ball and the Emergency Shelter 
                      cutscene.




That's all for this update, maybe I'll do weekly or bi weekly community posts with updates about Toing's Pops, and any further games in the series.

Foamy :O)

notes.title: Toing's Pops Version 1.0.1 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Toing's hearing radius was a bit higher than I liked, leading to him hearing you from far away.	
	- Made Toing's hearing radius smaller

A few bugs were found, so I fixed them. Obviously, why would I leave them?
	- Added collision to a few doors that you could walk through by accident
	- Removed a floating flashlight in the back room
	- Fixed the ending of the corrupted theme not being adjustable by the music slider


Ok, that's all. Let me know if you find any more bugs and I'll make sure to try and fix them. Thanks, tootles!
